title: GitLab CI/CD Pipelines
description: Configure automated pipelines in GitLab CI/CD with stages, variables, and deployment strategies.

data.text: **GitLab CI/CD** is a built-in continuous integration and delivery system integrated directly into GitLab. Pipelines are defined in a `.gitlab-ci.yml` file at the root of your repository, and they run automatically on GitLab's shared or your own runners.

terms.definition: A group of jobs executed by CI/CD, defined in .gitlab-ci.yml.
A single unit of work in the pipeline that runs a script.
A phase that groups jobs; jobs in the same stage run in parallel, stages run sequentially.
An agent that executes jobs. Can be shared, specific, or group-level.
Files generated by a job that are passed to later jobs or stored for download.

data.title: Complete pipeline definition
data.content: This pipeline builds, tests, and deploys a Node.js application in four stages.
data.code:
stages:
  - build
  - test
  - deploy-staging
  - deploy-production

variables:
  NODE_VERSION: '20'

cache:
  key: ${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}
  paths:
    - node_modules/

before_script:
  - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y nodejs
  - node --version
  - npm install -g npm@latest

build-job:
  stage: build
  image: node:${NODE_VERSION}
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npm run build
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - dist/
    expire_in: 1 day

unit-test:
  stage: test
  image: node:${NODE_VERSION}
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npm test
  artifacts:
    reports:
      junit: test-results.xml
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == 'merge_request_event'

data.text: Jobs listed in the same stage run in parallel, while stages run sequentially. This means your `test` jobs can all run at once, and `deploy` only starts after all tests pass.

data.caption: GitLab CI stages run sequentially; jobs within a stage run in parallel.

data.title: Defining and using variables
data.content: Variables in .gitlab-ci.yml and in the GitLab UI.
data.code:
variables:
  APP_NAME: 'my-app'
  REGISTRY: 'registry.gitlab.com'

build:
  script:
    - echo "Building ${APP_NAME}"
    - docker build -t ${REGISTRY}/${CI_PROJECT_PATH}:latest .

data.title: Types of variables
data.text: YAML-defined variables are visible to all. Protected variables only run on protected branches (e.g., main). Masked variables are hidden in logs. Add CI/CD variables in **Settings → CI/CD → Variables**.
GitLab environments track where your app is deployed (e.g., `staging`, `production`). You can use manual jobs and environment URLs to create approval gates.

data.title: Deploy to environments
data.content: Define environments with manual deployment gates.
data.code:
deploy-to-staging:
  stage: deploy-staging
  environment:
    name: staging
    url: https://staging.example.com
  script:
    - ./deploy.sh
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == 'main'

deploy-to-production:
  stage: deploy-production
  environment:
    name: production
    url: https://example.com
  script:
    - ./deploy.sh
  when: manual
  only:
    - tags

data.title: Set up a GitLab CI pipeline
data.description: Create and run a basic GitLab CI/CD pipeline from scratch.
steps: Create a `.gitlab-ci.yml` file in a GitLab repository.
Define a `stages:` list with build, test, and deploy stages.
Add a build job that installs dependencies and creates an artifact.
Add a test job that runs unit tests.
Add a deploy job marked as manual.
Push the file and monitor the pipeline in the GitLab UI.
Fix any failing jobs and verify the pipeline completes.
data.expectedOutcome: A working GitLab CI pipeline that builds, tests, and deploys your application.

data.title: GitHub Actions vs GitLab CI vs Jenkins

cards.title: GitHub Actions
cards.description: Pipelines as YAML in GitHub. Strong marketplace of reusable actions.

cards.title: GitLab CI
cards.description: Built-in to GitLab. Simple .gitlab-ci.yml with environments and MRs.

cards.title: Jenkins
cards.description: Self-hosted, plugin-heavy. Declarative pipelines with Jenkinsfile.

data.title: Choosing a platform
data.text: Pick based on where your code lives. If it's on GitHub, Actions is a natural fit. If you use GitLab, its built-in CI is convenient. Jenkins is best when you need maximum flexibility and control.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GitLab CI/CD uses `.gitlab-ci.yml` with stages, jobs, variables, cache, and artifacts.
Jobs in the same stage run in parallel; stages run sequentially.
Use protected and masked variables for security.
Environments and manual jobs create deployment gates.
Choose your CI/CD platform based on where your code and team live.
data.takeaway: All three major platforms solve the same problem; pick the one that fits your stack and workflows.
